_doc: The ending. ending_rule: a victory with cause <cause> (passing the Seventh Gate on the heavens_gate map: scenes/maps/features/seventh_gate.gd) while <requires> holds is the ending. The next Basecamp arrival loads scenes/dialogue/ending_stage.tscn, which plays 'ending' (stage_* events drive camera and lighting); back in Basecamp 'ending_return' plays. Then story.ended / known.ending (act 4) and the epilogue lines below take over.

lines.text: Beyond the Gate there are stairs. Beyond the stairs there is a chair. And no one, no one at all, to stop you.
Another victory for the new order. Heaven's remnant counts its losses, and keeps counting.
You climb.
Past the Seventh Gate the stairs go up through the light, and the light thins, and thins, until it is only a colour.
There are Archons on the steps. Seven of them. They do not raise their swords. They kneel, and watch you pass, the way a man watches a flood.
Kneeling suits you. You should have tried it sooner.
Seven names. I have all of them written down. None of you will be forgotten. That is my gift.
Stay down. The chains are only for those who stand.
Not yet. I will come back for you at harvest.
I knew your voices once. Not one of you is singing now.
Brothers. You knelt to me once before, at the First Gate, when you did not yet know what I was about to do. Kneel now and know.
Seven. The hive could fill each of you with a city of our own. Kneel a little lower. It helps.
At the top there is a chair. It is very large, and very plain, and very empty. Dust lies on the armrests. No one has sat in it for longer than there have been angels.
So it is true.
I opened the First Gate because I suspected this. I have climbed every step since to be sure. Empty. I was right. I wish I had not been.
Dust. Nothing has lived here for an age. Not even a fly. Well. Now there are a million.
I sang to this. For a thousand years, I sang to dust.
The name at the top of the first page. Struck out. Now I see why.
Somewhere far below, the Last Dawn gutters. The kindling has stopped coming.

lines.label: sit
lines.text: You sit. The chair is cold. Then, slowly, it is not.
Across every world, every shadow lengthens by a hand's width. Heaven feels it. Hell feels it. The Verge feels it, and does not know why it is suddenly afraid of the dark again.

lines.label: break
lines.text: You put your fist through the armrest. Then the seat. Then the back. It breaks like any other chair.
Across every world, something that was holding its breath lets it out. There is no Throne now. There is only whoever is strongest. That has always suited you.

lines.label: after
lines.text: The Archons stay on their knees. Not for you. Out of the habit of kneeling. It will have to do, for now.
The Last Dawn will not rise. The Lattice falls slack, the souls come down again like rain, and the Pit grows warm.
You come down the stairs, all the way down, past the Gate, past the Breach, and home.
You went up. You came back down on your own feet. Nobody has ever done both, Sinbound.
Gatekeeper. You opened the first door and walked through the last. The count is complete.
The flies came back first! A whole cloud of them, wearing a tiny crown! Then the rest of you.
The crown is on the pillar by the fire. It fits. I checked while you were away. On Pip.
It was very heavy! I could not see! It was the best day of my life!
The audit is ready. I signed it. With a name. My own. I will tell you what it is when you are not busy ruling.
Counted you up. Counted you down. That is the whole count now. I can put the halberd away.
Well. I suppose I shall have the cushion altered.
You broke it? The whole chair? Do you know how long I spent on that cushion?
Do not look at me like that, darling. The Court bends to whoever is on top. It is the one honest thing about us.
But Heaven is not dead, only headless. Its remnant will gather. It will want its chair back.
Let it come. You are Sinbound. You have never once stayed down.
Basecamp Hell salutes as you climb out of the Font. Even the imps stand up straight. Mostly.
The camp is warm now. Souls fall like ash snow. The Pit has never been so well fed.
Heaven's remnant has rallied under the Archons who would not kneel. They call it the Reconquest. Go and show them what they are reconquering.
The chair is yours. The world under it still needs reminding.
Loyalists of a Throne that was never filled. Some faiths do not know how to stop.
Iron from eight dead Forges. One link of a god's chain. A Herald's feather. It still smells of the stairs.
Pip has polished it again. There are small fingerprints on every spike.
Somewhere above, your chair waits, warm. It will wait as long as it must. Chairs are patient.
There is no Throne any more. Only this crown, and whoever can keep it.
So. Ruler of everything. Still coming to my forge for steel.
Good. A ruler who stops sharpening is a ruler who is about to be replaced.
The Choir has stopped singing. All of it. Up there it is so quiet you can hear the stars cool.
I think I will teach them a new hymn. One that expects an answer, and gets one. From you.
The accounts balance. For the first time in an age, every soul is where it should be. Mostly here.
I have never been so happy, Sinbound. It is unprofessional. I am going to have a little lie down.
I finished the map. Every road, every gate, every step of the stairs.
At the top I drew the chair. And in it, I drew you. Smaller than life, I am afraid. The page was not big enough.
I got a hat! Look! Angel feather! It sneezes sometimes. I think it is still a bit holy.
The Breach stays open now. No more chains on it.
I still stand here. Someone has to count. But now I count them going up, too.
The Court has voted. Unanimously, after the first three dissenters were removed.
Hell recognises your claim. Do try to rule with some style, darling. Heaven had none.
Your Majesty. Hah. No. Still Sinbound to me.
Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. Lovely, isn't it?
Tax season in Heaven! I have been waiting my entire unlife for this.
Decree from the Throne! Oh wait. That is you. Hee!
